findings.summary: SidebarProvider writes sidebar_state cookie on every toggle but never reads it back on mount; sidebar always resets to expanded (defaultOpen=true) on any full page navigation
findings.failure_scenario: User collapses the sidebar, then navigates from one project to another (or from project to account page). The SidebarProvider re-mounts, `_open` is initialized to `defaultOpen=true`, and the sidebar reopens. The cookie intended to persist state across sessions is never consumed.

findings.summary: Separator element in sidebarLinks.map() lacks a `key` prop, causing React reconciliation warnings
findings.failure_scenario: The ProjectSidebarLayout passes footerSidebarLinks containing a {separator:true} item. When RenderSidebarGroup maps over this array, the separator returns `<SidebarSeparator className='my-1' />` with no key. React logs a warning. If separators were ever reordered, DOM state (focus, animations) could become mismatched.

findings.summary: SidebarMenuSkeleton uses Math.random() inside useMemo during render, causing SSR hydration mismatch
findings.failure_scenario: Server renders skeleton with random width '67%', client hydrates with random width '82%'. React logs a hydration mismatch error and may re-render the component, causing a visible layout flicker. The component is currently unused but exported from the module.

findings.summary: Separator element in RenderSidebarLinks lacks a `key` prop, same defect as in RenderSidebarGroup
findings.failure_scenario: If any consumer of RenderSidebarLinks (mobile sidebar, contract page layouts) adds a separator to its links array, React will warn about missing keys.

findings.summary: prefetch={false} added globally to all NavLink instances, disabling Next.js link prefetching for every sidebar navigation link
findings.failure_scenario: Users hover over sidebar links or scroll them into viewport; Next.js no longer prefetches the target page's JS and data. On click, the user experiences a full network round-trip delay instead of an instant client-side transition. Affects all consumers: CustomSidebar, FullWidthSidebarLayout, and the nebula app's ChatSidebarLink.

findings.summary: RenderSidebarGroup does not render an external-link icon for links with http-prefixed hrefs, unlike the old RenderSidebarLinks which renders ExternalLinkIcon
findings.failure_scenario: In the new project sidebar, 'Documentation' and 'Playground' links (hrefs: https://portal.thirdweb.com, https://playground.thirdweb.com/...) appear identical to internal links. The old sidebar always showed an ExternalLinkIcon next to external links. Users cannot visually distinguish internal from external navigation targets in the new sidebar.

findings.summary: Cookie set without SameSite or Secure attributes; sidebar_state cookie is sent on cross-site requests where it should not be
findings.failure_scenario: On a cross-origin request to the application, the sidebar_state cookie is attached to the request. While the value ('true'/'false') is non-sensitive, the lack of SameSite=Lax means CSRF-style side effects could be possible in some configurations.

findings.summary: MobileSidebarTrigger creates a new array reference [...contentSidebarLinks, ...(footerSidebarLinks || [])] on every render, defeating the useMemo inside useActiveSidebarLink
findings.failure_scenario: On every re-render of FullWidthSidebarLayout, useActiveSidebarLink receives a new array reference, causing its internal useMemo to re-run and re-scan all links even when neither contentSidebarLinks nor footerSidebarLinks have changed.
